cards.front: Which homologous series has the functional group -COOH?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids.

cards.front: What is the functional group of an alcohol?
cards.back: An -OH group bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

cards.front: Which homologous series contains a carbon-nitrogen triple bond?
cards.back: Nitriles. The carbon atom of the nitrile group is bonded to the rest of the molecule.

cards.front: Which class of compounds includes molecules with an -NH₂ group bonded to an alkyl group?
cards.back: Primary amines.

cards.front: What is the name of the -CH₃ substituent?
cards.back: Methyl.

cards.front: What is the structural formula of propane?
cards.back: CH₃CH₂CH₃

cards.front: What is the molecular formula of hex-1-ene?
cards.back: C₆H₁₂

cards.front: What suffix is used when naming a carboxylic acid?
cards.back: The suffix is -oic acid, as in ethanoic acid.

cards.front: What ending is used for the acid-derived part of an ester name?
cards.back: The ending is -oate, as in ethyl ethanoate.

cards.front: What suffix and prefix are used to name an -OH group?
cards.back:
The suffix is -ol, as in ethanol.
The prefix is hydroxy- when a higher-priority functional group determines the suffix.

cards.front: How is an ester written in structural formula notation using R groups?
cards.back:
RCOOR′
R and R′ represent organic groups that may be different.

cards.front: What class of compounds has the structure R–O–R′?
cards.back: Ethers.

cards.front: What is the structural difference between an aldehyde and a ketone?
cards.back:
An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon bonded to at least one H atom: -CHO.
A ketone has a carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbon atoms.

cards.front: What is the functional group of an alkene?
cards.back: A carbon-carbon double bond, C=C.

cards.front: What type of carbon-carbon bonds are present in an alkane?
cards.back: Single covalent bonds only.

cards.front: What group is present in both aldehydes and ketones?
cards.back: The carbonyl group, C=O.

cards.front: What suffix is used when naming a ketone?
cards.back: The suffix is -one, as in propanone.

cards.front: What suffix is used when naming an aldehyde?
cards.back: The suffix is -al, as in ethanal.

cards.front: What is a functional group?
cards.back: An atom or group of atoms responsible for the characteristic chemical reactions of an organic compound.

cards.front: What is a homologous series?
cards.back: A series of organic compounds having the same functional group, with each successive member differing by CH₂.

cards.front: What does a displayed formula show?
cards.back:
The relative positioning of atoms and the bonds between them.
Every atom and every bond is shown.

cards.front: How do you choose the numbering direction when naming a simple branched alkane?
cards.back:
Number the parent chain to give the branches the lowest possible set of numbers.
Compare the sets at the first point where they differ.

cards.front: How do you choose the parent chain of a simple branched alkane?
cards.back:
Choose the longest continuous carbon chain.
The number of carbon atoms in that chain determines the stem of the name.

cards.front: What does R represent in an organic formula?
cards.back: An alkyl group or another fragment of an organic compound that is not involved in the reaction.

cards.front: What is an alkyl group?
cards.back:
A group formed by removing one H atom from an alkane.
For example, methane gives the methyl group, -CH₃.

cards.front: What is a haloalkane?
cards.back: A compound formed when one or more H atoms in an alkane are replaced by halogen atoms.

cards.front: Which homologous series has the functional group –COCl?
cards.back: Acyl chlorides.

cards.front: What is an alkane?
cards.back:
A saturated, acyclic hydrocarbon.
It contains only carbon and hydrogen, with single bonds only.

cards.front: What ending is used when naming an acyl chloride?
cards.back: The ending is -oyl chloride, as in ethanoyl chloride.

cards.front: What is a general formula?
cards.back:
The simplest algebraic formula of a member of a homologous series.
For alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

cards.front: What is an empirical formula?
cards.back: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.

cards.front: What is a molecular formula?
cards.back: The actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule.

cards.front: What does a structural formula show?
cards.back:
The minimal detail that shows the arrangement of atoms in a molecule.
For example, CH₃CH₂OH is the structural formula of ethanol.
